questions.prompt: How does Ship It keep learner code away from the host app and the network, and where does that isolation stop?

keyPoints.text: A compiler worker transpiles learner code and injects time guards, so learner source never runs on the host thread.
keyPoints.quote: Learner source never executes on the host application thread.

keyPoints.text: The iframe is sandboxed with allow-scripts and allow-forms only: no same-origin, navigation, download or popups.
keyPoints.quote: without same-origin, top-navigation, download, or popup permissions

keyPoints.text: Pure-function tickets run in a blob worker created by the iframe, which inherits its CSP and has network and nested-worker APIs disabled.
keyPoints.quote: The worker inherits the iframe’s CSP, has no DOM, and has network and nested-worker APIs disabled.

keyPoints.text: The host accepts a result only from that iframe's window and with the run's random id.
keyPoints.quote: The host accepts a result only from that iframe's window and with the run's random id

keyPoints.text: It is a learning sandbox, not a hostile-code judge: hidden tests and references ship to the client and can be inspected.
keyPoints.quote: This is a local learning sandbox, not a hostile-code judging service.

keyPoints.text: In iframe mode learner code shares the document with the bridge and could post its own result.
keyPoints.quote: In iframe mode, learner code shares the document with the bridge script, so it can in principle post its own result.

questions.prompt: Why are there several separate time limits in the runner, and what does each one catch?

keyPoints.text: Compilation has its own 30 second limit.
Sandbox start-up is bounded separately at 10 seconds.
Execution gets 3 seconds counted from the frame's ready message.
keyPoints.quote: execution 3 s from the frame's `ready` message

keyPoints.text: An in-sandbox guard throws after 2.5 seconds inside instrumented loops and functions.
keyPoints.quote: an in-sandbox guard that throws after 2.5 s inside instrumented loops and functions

keyPoints.text: A while(true) loop is stopped by the harness guard message, while a promise that never settles hits the host's 3 second message.
keyPoints.quote: a `while (true) {}` loop fails with the harness message

keyPoints.text: Cancelling or navigating removes the frame and terminates its worker.
keyPoints.quote: Cancellation or navigation removes the frame and terminates its worker.

questions.prompt: How are progress and rewards protected from farming and forgery, and why is that protection deliberately limited?

keyPoints.text: Progress is stored locally under a versioned key.
Imported results are rejected if a test name is not one of the ticket's known names.
keyPoints.quote: imported results are rejected if any name is not one of the ticket's `testNames`

keyPoints.text: Rerunning the same passing code does not change the XP total.
keyPoints.quote: rerun the same passing code twice; the total does not change

keyPoints.text: The store's name check limits forged results to known test names rather than preventing them.
keyPoints.quote: the store's name check (`store.ts:337,504`) limits forgeries to known test names

keyPoints.text: Tamper resistance is an explicit non-goal of this offline tool.
keyPoints.quote: This is consistent with the stated non-goal (progress is not tamper-resistant)

keyPoints.text: Streaks keep one lifetime grace day.
keyPoints.quote: streak with one lifetime grace day
